city_center.name: Downtown Jackson (Farish Street Historic District) + Mississippi Farmers Market
city_center.landmark: Farish Street Historic District (one of the largest historically African-American business districts in the US) and the Old Capitol; Mississippi Farmers Market on High Street
city_center.notes: Mississippi capital in the Delta-and-Piney-Woods transition. Kroger and Winn-Dixie serve the metro; Rouses has expanded from Louisiana into Mississippi. Farish Street was a hub of Black-owned business and blues heritage. sources: general Farish Street heritage; Mississippi Farmers Market (MDAC).

cultural_notes: Jackson is Mississippi's capital, sitting at the transition between the Delta to the northwest and the Piney Woods to the south (source: general regional knowledge; language selection flagged INFERRED)

The Farish Street Historic District was one of the largest historically African-American business districts in the US and a center of blues and civil-rights history; reference it respectfully and never trivialize it (source: general historical knowledge -- honor gravity, no trivializing)

Mississippi's growing season supports strong summer vegetables (tomatoes, sweet corn, okra) and a substantial fall sweet-potato crop, plus spring strawberries and asparagus (source: msstate.edu Extension Buy Fresh Fruits and Vegetables in Season; texasrealfood.com Mississippi)
Kroger and Winn-Dixie anchor the metro grocery landscape, with Rouses expanding from Louisiana (source: regional retail footprint)
